body.statement: For every rational interior one-mechanism affine family, the following are equivalent: \(\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}\) with \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\); and \(\operatorname{rank}([E_T;b_T])>\operatorname{rank}(E_T)\). The condition is independent of the rational basis \(R_T\). Whenever it holds, rational row reduction yields \(v=R_Tq\), and there is a computable \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) such that every \(t\in\mathbb Q\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\) keeps \(\theta+t v\) normalized and strictly positive, preserves the entire normalized selected observational law and \(D_{\rho}\) exactly, and changes \(N_{\rho}\). Thus \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns a positive rational pair certifying nonidentification of \(\psi\) in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations, and \(\operatorname{Verify}\) checks the expanded certificate in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.
body.justification: The theorem turns a numerical or symbolic fiber direction into an exact, portable, positive rational causal nonidentification certificate.
body.gap: Discrete polynomial programs describe observational fibers, but the checked literature does not isolate an exact simplex-tangent criterion that simultaneously locks a selected conditional denominator and separates its numerator.
body.consumer: A graph search or algebraic solver can hand one passing template to the compiler and obtain a certificate that a third party verifies without trusting the search.
